A Guy With A Scarf research/Automated match video/Premium edition/Once Sport (Once Sport d.o.o.)

Club pays for a coaching tool

Once Sport (Once Sport d.o.o.)Premium

Zagreb, Croatia · founded 2011 · active · once.sport/autocam · last verified 2026-09-19

Club pays for a coaching toolSoftware onlyDeployed in ItalyEvidence AUnder €500 to start

Desktop software from a Zagreb video analysis company that turns wide-angle footage from a Reolink camera, two GoPros or any panoramic source into an auto-followed broadcast-style video, with live streaming to YouTube and an optional €5 per match cloud processing service.

For Coaches, analysts and small clubs that already own or can buy a cheap wide-angle camera and a reasonable PC, and who want automated match video for a few tens of euros a month, with no proprietary camera or locked cloud. Football academies in Portugal, Spain, Croatia, the UK and Italy make up the visible user base.

Once Sport exists because a video analysis software house realised that the expensive part of a Veo or Pixellot is the proprietary camera and cloud, and that a good tracking model running on the coach's own laptop could deliver the same virtual camera from commodity hardware [once-sport-01, once-sport-07]. It matters now because at €19 or €38 a month with hardware you source yourself, and €5 a match in the cloud, it undercuts every integrated system by an order of magnitude at the moment budgets at amateur clubs are being squeezed [once-sport-03]. It tells you that automated match video is being unbundled into camera, processing and platform, and that the processing layer is on its way to becoming a cheap software subscription.

Price band €19/month Autocam Personal or €38/month Autocam Club, tax excluded, yearly billing at nine times the monthly rate; €5 per match cloud processing; camera hardware bought separately once-sport-03

Italy AS Lodigiani Calcio 1972 in Rome uses Autocam, Analyser and Coach Board across its academy and first team per a March 2025 case study, the software ships with an Italian interface and pricing table, and the company exhibited at The Coach Experience in Rimini in June 2025 [once-sport-08, once-sport-03, once-sport-06].

The verdict

Look if You have someone at the club who is comfortable with a Windows PC, an SD card and a tripod, you already use or want Once Sport Analyser, and you want automated match video for a fraction of the cost of an integrated camera. Look also if privacy matters, since the offline version processes footage on your own computer and nothing leaves the building unless you stream it.

Skip if You want a camera you bolt to a pole and forget, with someone else responsible when the recording fails, because Once Sport sells software and leaves hardware, mounting, power and connectivity to you. Skip also if you need fan monetisation, paywalls or sponsor management, or if your match video must be ready minutes after the final whistle without a capable PC on site.

Watch-outs

  • Processing time on the offline version depends on your computer, and the Italian case study reports 65 to 70 minutes for a match, so budget for a decent GPU or use the €5 cloud option with a 24-hour turnaround [once-sport-08, once-sport-03].
  • Hardware is never included: the fixed option lists an 8K 20 fps IP67 camera with PoE and the portable option a 4K 20 fps IP67 camera or two action cameras on a 6-metre tripod, and Once Sport publishes no prices for any of it [once-sport-01].
  • Autocam Personal caps processing at 40 hours a month and three tagged football matches, and Autocam Club allows six tagged matches, so the automatic tagging component is metered even on the unlimited-hours plan [once-sport-03].
  • The 20 fps capture rate of the recommended cameras is below the 25 to 30 fps that broadcast-style output normally uses, which affects motion smoothness in the final video [once-sport-01].
  • The terms of service list Analyser and Coach Board by name and do not mention Autocam or the cloud processing service, and they place jurisdiction in England while stating the company is based in Croatia, so contractual coverage of match footage in the cloud tier is unclear [once-sport-04].
  • The company is a three-owner Croatian d.o.o. with no public financials, so support depth for a global user base of 5,000 or more claimed coaches rests on a small team [once-sport-09, once-sport-05].

Products

  • Once Sport Autocam (offline) (app). Windows desktop software that auto-follows the action from wide-angle footage, stitches dual action cameras, controls Reolink cameras and streams live to RTMP. [src: once-sport-07]
  • Once Sport Autocam Cloud (platform). Per-match cloud processing at €5 with 24-hour turnaround for clubs without a capable PC. [src: once-sport-03]
  • Once Sport Analyser (app). Video analysis and telestration software in Basic, Pro and Elite tiers, with Basic bundled into Autocam plans. [src: once-sport-03]
  • Once Sport Coach Board (app). Tactical board and drill animation tool, free in Basic and €3 a month in Pro, bundled with Autocam plans. [src: once-sport-03]

Profile against the 24 criteria

Use-case fit
Autocam serves clubs that want automated match and training video from their own camera, on full-size and small-sided pitches from 5v5 to 11v11, across football, basketball, handball, futsal and more, with Analyser Basic and Coach Board bundled into the subscription since July 2025 [once-sport-01, once-sport-10]. Visible users are academies and semi-professional clubs such as HNK Vukovar 1991, ACD Carapeços and AS Lodigiani [once-sport-05, once-sport-11, once-sport-08]. It fits a coach-led workflow and does not fit a club that wants a hands-off streaming service.
Capture quality
Output quality depends on the source: the vendor's fixed recipe is an 8K, 20 fps, IP67 camera on PoE and the portable recipe a 4K, 20 fps, IP67 camera or two GoPro or DJI action cameras on a 6-metre tripod, with the software cropping a broadcast-style frame from the wide image [once-sport-01]. November 2025's version 3.0 added Reolink camera control and automatic stitching of two action cameras into one wide-angle source [once-sport-07]. Sample footage from Germany, the UK and Scotland is published on the Autocam page, and the 20 fps ceiling of the recommended cameras is the main quality constraint [once-sport-01].
Automation accuracy
The software uses neural networks and computer vision to digitally pan and zoom in imitation of a camera operator, with automatic field marking, tilt correction and adjustable zoom settings in the 3.0 processing setup [once-sport-01, once-sport-07]. Football matches can be automatically tagged, metered at three or six per month depending on plan [once-sport-03]. No accuracy figures or independent tests are published, and the Lodigiani analyst's description of television-like precision is the strongest public endorsement [once-sport-08].
Multi-angle and stitching
Dual-camera processing stitches left and right action camera footage into a single wide-angle video without manual syncing, and the company offers a printable dual-GoPro mount design on request [once-sport-07, once-sport-01]. Single panoramic sources from Reolink are handled directly. There is no support for combining more than two sources or for cutting between separate angles.
Latency and live readiness
Autocam can stream the processed feed live to YouTube or any RTMP platform while the match happens, with stream URL and key entered separately in the 3.0 interface, and live streaming to YouTube is included in both subscriptions [once-sport-01, once-sport-07, once-sport-03]. Live processing requires a capable computer at the pitch connected to the camera. The Portuguese club ACD Carapeços is presented as a live streaming case [once-sport-11]. No latency figure is published.
Reliability and resilience
Because recording happens on the camera's SD card or the action cameras' storage and processing happens afterwards, a failed upload or PC crash does not lose the match footage [once-sport-07, once-sport-01]. Reliability of the recording itself depends on the user's hardware and setup. No app store ratings or independent reliability reviews exist, since the product is desktop software.
Portability and install
The portable recipe is a 4K camera or two action cameras on a 6-metre tripod with a 12V power bank giving six hours and a waterproof bag, carried and set up by the club, and the Lodigiani academy uses this kit across home and away pitches [once-sport-01, once-sport-08]. The fixed recipe needs PoE and either the venue network or a router [once-sport-01]. Once Sport supplies instructions and software, the club supplies everything else.
Connectivity and bandwidth
Offline processing needs no internet at all, streaming needs a live uplink from the pitch-side PC, and the cloud tier needs the wide-angle file uploaded for a 24-hour turnaround [once-sport-01, once-sport-03]. No bandwidth figures are published. This is the least connectivity-dependent option in this group.
Workflow and UX
The 3.0 release reorganised the desktop app into Source, Processing Setup and Destination tabs, with Reolink live preview, clip search and direct import, and processed video can be exported to any analysis platform [once-sport-07, once-sport-01]. Analyser Basic, Coach Board and, since December 2025, full Autocam integration inside Analyser reduce the number of tools a coach juggles [once-sport-10, once-sport-06]. It remains a desktop workflow that assumes a PC operator.
Analysis layer
Autocam subscriptions bundle Analyser Basic with professional tagging, telestration, basic automatic tracking, field mapping and basic export, and Coach Board for drills and tactical animation, with Analyser Pro at €36 and Elite at €72 a month as upgrades [once-sport-03, once-sport-10]. Automatic football tagging is metered per plan [once-sport-03]. Analyser is used by national teams, Dinamo Zagreb U19, Paris FC's women's centre and Arena Sport Slovenia, which gives the analysis layer stronger references than the camera layer [once-sport-05].
Integrations
Processed video exports to any analysis platform, live output goes to YouTube and RTMP destinations, Reolink cameras are controlled natively and Coach Board projects exchange XML [once-sport-01, once-sport-07, once-sport-03]. Analyser imports CSV since November 2025 [once-sport-06]. There is no API and no club management or OTT integration.
Distribution and OTT
Distribution is limited to a live stream to YouTube or another RTMP platform with sponsor logos and match results overlaid by Autocam [once-sport-01, once-sport-03]. There is no paywall, viewer app or highlight publishing product. Clubs monetise through their own YouTube channel or a third-party platform.
Data access and ownership
Footage stays on the club's camera storage and PC in the offline version, output is a standard video file, and the vendor states that videos remain private with offline functionality [once-sport-01]. The cloud per-match service requires uploading footage, and the published terms cover Analyser and Coach Board content rules without addressing Autocam cloud processing, retention or reuse [once-sport-04]. Ownership is strong in practice for offline users and undocumented for cloud users.
Privacy and compliance
Offline processing means no personal data leaves the club unless it chooses to stream, which is the cleanest privacy posture in this group [once-sport-01]. The privacy policy covers account data and cookies, and there is no guidance on consent for filming minors or any blurring tool [once-sport-04]. Compliance for the footage itself therefore rests with the club.
Security
Not assessable from public sources. The terms describe the company as based in Croatia and name no hosting provider or certification for the cloud service [once-sport-04].
Pricing and TCO
Autocam Personal is €19 a month or €171 a year and Autocam Club €38 a month or €342 a year, with yearly billing at nine times the monthly rate, USD equivalents of 23 and 46 a month, and cloud processing at €5 or USD 6 per match with packages such as 3+1 and 6+3, all tax excluded [once-sport-03]. Hardware is extra and unpriced by the vendor; a Reolink 8K PoE camera or two action cameras plus a 6-metre tripod and power bank are the stated inputs [once-sport-01]. A club buying its own kit can plausibly be running for under €1,000 in year one plus the subscription, which is the lowest entry cost among the vendors covered.
Support and service
Support and updates are included in every subscription, a video analyst certification course comes with yearly plans, and the company runs a free trial and Calendly calls [once-sport-03, once-sport-01]. Testimonials praise the customer support team as very helpful [once-sport-05]. No SLA is published and the team is small.
Company health and roadmap
Once Sport d.o.o. was founded in 2011 in Zagreb, is owned by Dalibor Čvek, Ivica Petrović and Nenad Markuš with Čvek and Markuš as directors, and publishes no financials [once-sport-09]. The blog shows a release roughly every month through 2025 and 2026, including Autocam 3.0 in November 2025, full Autocam integration into Analyser in December 2025 and a redesigned Coach Board and multitrack review in August 2026, alongside a heavy event schedule across Europe, the USA, Southeast Asia and Tunisia [once-sport-06, once-sport-07]. Cadence is the health signal; capital is unknown.
Evidence and references
Autocam references include AS Lodigiani Calcio 1972 in Italy, HNK Vukovar 1991's academy, ACD Carapeços in Portugal and FC Ferreiras, while Analyser references include the Croatian national futsal team, Dinamo Zagreb U19, Paris FC, Plymouth Argyle, Greenock Morton, SK Interobal Plzeň, Estoril Praia, SV Sandhausen and FFF Pays de la Loire coach education [once-sport-05, once-sport-08, once-sport-11, once-sport-06]. The company claims 5,000 or more coaches, analysts and clubs worldwide [once-sport-05]. No independent test of Autocam output exists.
Coach and analyst satisfaction
Testimonials from analysts at Dinamo Zagreb, Paris FC, Sporting Braga and national team coaches praise ease of use, price and support, and the Lodigiani analyst calls Autocam revolutionary for combining automated recording with television-style framing [once-sport-05, once-sport-08]. These are vendor-selected quotes, and no third-party review site carries meaningful ratings. Sentiment is positive and thinly evidenced.
Edge versus cloud
Autocam is edge by design, with processing on the club's own PC and an optional cloud tier at €5 per match for those without the hardware or the patience, and the choice is the customer's per match [once-sport-01, once-sport-03]. Processing time on the edge depends on the PC, with 65 to 70 minutes reported for a match in the Italian case [once-sport-08]. Live streaming requires the edge PC at the venue.
Accessibility and languages
The software, pricing table and site run in English, German, French, Portuguese, Spanish and Italian, with a currency toggle between EUR and USD [once-sport-03, once-sport-01]. That makes Once Sport one of the few vendors in this database with a native Italian interface.
Upgrade path
A user can move from the €5 per match cloud tier to Personal to Club, add Analyser Pro or Elite and Coach Board Pro, and upgrade hardware from action cameras to a fixed 8K Reolink without changing software [once-sport-03, once-sport-01]. Plans can be upgraded or downgraded and cancelled on the pricing page terms [once-sport-02]. Software updates are included.
Differentiators worth testing
Run the same match through the offline version on your own laptop and through the €5 cloud tier, compare output quality and time to delivery, and check the automatic football tagging against your own count [once-sport-03]. Test the dual-GoPro stitching on a small-sided pitch, since that is the cheapest possible entry [once-sport-07]. Confirm in writing what the cloud service does with uploaded footage, because the published terms do not say [once-sport-04].

Company

Ownership and funding Once Sport d.o.o., OIB 22886137161, Remetinečka cesta 7, Zagreb, founded 2011, owned by Dalibor Čvek, Ivica Petrović and Nenad Markuš, with Čvek and Markuš as directors [once-sport-09]. No external funding is public.

Financials Not public. Croatian registry portals hold accounts behind a paywall and the vendor discloses nothing [once-sport-09].

Scale, company-stated Vendor-stated: trusted by 5,000 or more coaches, analysts and clubs worldwide as of September 2026 [once-sport-05].
